'''Andrew Jeffrey Gunion Barclay''' (19 April 1849 – 15 September 1943) was a Scottish [[mathematician]], known for being one of the founders of the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]].

== Life and work ==
Barclay studied at [[University of Edinburgh]] where he graduated in mathematics in 1880.<ref>{{smallcaps|O'Connor & Robertson}}, MacTutor History of Mathematics.</ref> Then he was professor of mathematics at [[George Watson's College]] (Edinburgh) and at [[High School of Glasgow]].{{sfn | Rankin | 1983 | p=144 }} He retired in 1914 and went to reside in London with a son.

Barclay, with [[Alexander Yule Fraser]] and [[Cargill Gilston Knott]], issued in January 1883 a circular calling for a Mathematical Society.{{sfn | Despeaux | 2011 | p=172 }} That year the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]] was founded and Barclay became its president in 1884.
